title: Getting Started with AI for Rapid Software Development for Business Central
summary: Shows a simple AI-assisted workflow for Business Central projects. Copilot Chat pulls functional requirements out of a sample meeting transcript for a fictional space travel agency that needs usage-based asset depreciation and launch costing. A second prompt then turns those requirements into a Business Central functional design document that identifies the extension development needed.
key_points: Functional requirements describe what the system must do, not how, and should be testable as yes or no statements; Copilot Chat is well suited to extracting them from transcripts or emails.
The example system groups reusable assets into LaunchEvents, depreciates them by time and by usage, handles refurbishment capitalisation and allocates mission costs.
Business Central serves as the GL and invoicing system, with batched journal posting, a two-way sync and full audit traceability back to telemetry and approvals.
The functional design prompt adds product specifics, and the AL Development Collection extension supplies helpful boilerplate.

quotes.text: AI Assisted Software Development promises faster, more accurate, and more feature rich software at fewer hours of labor.
quotes.why_it_matters: Sets expectation for using AI to accelerate both requirements extraction and functional design phases of software projects

quotes.text: We'll design a bi‑directional sync: asset master and depreciation schedules flow to BC, and vendor invoices/payments flow back.
quotes.why_it_matters: Shows how a specialized asset accounting system integrates with Business Central as the GL and invoicing source of truth
